_source: Polled live on 2026-08-29 against the founder's own TPT seller session: the `TaxCodesQuery`, `EducationStandardsJurisdictionsQuery` and `MyProductListingsCustomCategories` operations on https://www.teacherspayteachers.com/graph/graphql, the `JSON.parse` blobs embedded in the `tpt-frontend` webpack chunks, and the `var cfg = {...}` bootstrap on GET /My-Products/New/Digital-Next. taxonomyTags.note: One flat slug namespace where a grade, a subject, a resource type, a file format and a language are all the same kind of thing; only `category` tells them apart, and it is metadata about the slug rather than a separate field on the product. Referentially closed: every `parentId` resolves inside the set. Max depth 2.
taxonomyTags.hiddenNote: An `isHidden` facet is a retired value that still reads back on existing products. Accept it on read, never offer it on write.
taxonomyTags.writableNote: A `sellerWritable: false` facet is one the create form offers no control for, so the projection must never post it. The 2026-09-03 DOM read renders seventeen Grade-Level checkboxes against the twenty Grade-Level facets here: `elementary`, `middle-school` and `high-school` are the buyer-side roll-ups that drive browse filters and are parents of the seventeen. Distinct from `isHidden`, which is a retired value: a roll-up is current and unwritable rather than retired.

teachingDuration.note: The write side posts the id and the GraphQL read side returns the symbolic name. `UNKNOWN` appears in the read-side label map with no numeric counterpart, so it is a read sentinel rather than a member. The DOM index equals the id for all twenty-three, and the DOM is the display authority for the labels: sixteen were corrected to its title case on 2026-09-03 (ids 0, 13, 14, 15, 19, 20 and 22 already matched). answerKey.note: `UNKNOWN` is again read-side only. The 2026-09-03 DOM read confirms all six labels and settles that the menu order is not the id order: the six `li` elements run N/A, Included, Not Included, Included with Rubric, Rubric Only, Does Not Apply, which is ids 0, 1, 2, 4, 5, 3. The `li` elements carry no value attribute, so an id inferred from a menu position writes Included with Rubric as Does Not Apply. Read the id from this file, never from a position. Source: docs/research/rethink/tpt-create-form-dom.md, read from a full-page DOM snapshot of GET /My-Products/New/Digital-Next taken 2026-09-03.

copyrightDeclaration.note: A legal attestation of authorship, so it is posted only where the seller has made one and never as a constant. The chunk-1564 form wiring names the group `data[Item][...]` where the captured writes posted `data[ItemsProperty][...]`; the captured wire is authoritative for the path and the two members are the same either way.

statusUser.note: Draft versus live is a field rather than a route: the captured create posted 0 and the captured edit 1.

audience.note: A separate scalar from the `audience`-category facets in `taxonomyTags`. `OTHER` pairs with a free-text `audienceText`. Neither captured write posted this field.

itemType.note: Chosen on the create-type page (`page-CreateProductSelectTypePage`) rather than in a dropdown on the form. Only DIGITAL_PRODUCT occurs across this seller's 154 products.

educationStandardsJurisdictions.api: EducationStandardsQuery($id: ID!, $depth: Int) expands one jurisdiction into a flat list carrying id, name, depth, notation, grades, type, parentIds, sequence, categorySequence, descriptionText and descriptionHtml
educationStandardsJurisdictions.note: The form field takes a standard id from a leaf below one of these roots, not a jurisdiction id. Full expansion across all 166 runs to thousands of nodes and is expanded on demand instead. Verified live against Common Core (id 3054): depth=1 returns 2 nodes of `type: subject`, depth=2 returns 49 (those 2 plus 47 of `type: domain`). 28 of the 166 carry a `notation`.

selectionCaps._note: How many members each create-form picker states it accepts. The form states these as placeholder and helper text rather than as a `max` attribute, and the 2026-09-03 DOM read confirms no `max`, `maxlength` or data attribute anywhere on the four controls. A picker named in `contradictedByCapture` has been observed to accept more than it states: the 2026-08-30 create posted four PreK-12-Subject-Area slugs against a stated cap of three, so that number is the form's claim rather than a refusal, and enforcing it would raise a question about a set the platform already accepted. A cap absent here is unmeasured, never unlimited.

constraints.note: Every value but the title length comes from the `var cfg` bootstrap the create page hands its own client, so these are the client's bounds and not server refusals anyone measured. 80 is both the title-length constant in chunk `tpt-frontend.1.1564` and the longest of 352 observed titles; the counting unit is unverified, so `crates/tam-domain/src/registry.rs` declares no title cap.

notFound.licence: TPT has no licence field and no CC-style licence vocabulary at all. The nearest levers are `copyrightDeclaration` and the multiple-license price, which is a pricing mechanism rather than a rights grant.
notFound.productCategory: There is no separate product-category or subject select. What a seller picks as a subject is a `taxonomyTags` facet with `category: PreK-12-Subject-Area`, and a resource type is one with `category: Type-of-Resource`.
notFound.countryId: The read side returns `countryId: 153` and a `countryIdFlag`; the country vocabulary itself was not found in any chunk.
notFound.status: `status`, `statusAdmin` and `statusCopyright` read ACTIVE across this store's 154 products and are single-valued in the sample, so no set is on file.
